desc:
A fence has posts posts in a row. Each post is painted with one of colors available colors. To keep the fence interesting, no three consecutive posts may share the same color (two in a row are fine).

Return the number of valid paintings, modulo 1,000,000,007.

Example: posts = 3, colors = 2 gives 6 (the 8 paintings minus the all-same ones AAA and BBB).
hints: Count by the end of the fence. A valid painting either ends with two equal colors or with two different ones.
Track same = paintings whose last two posts match, diff = paintings whose last two posts differ.
Next post: new_same = diff (copy the last color, allowed only if the previous two differed); new_diff = (same + diff) * (colors - 1). Start with same = 0, diff = colors for one post.
editorial: After painting i posts, classify each valid painting by whether the last two posts have equal colors (same) or different colors (diff). To extend by one post: repeating the last color is legal only if the last two posts differ, otherwise we would get three in a row, so new_same = diff. Choosing a different color is always legal, in colors - 1 ways, from either state, so new_diff = (same + diff) * (colors - 1).

With one post there are colors paintings and no pair yet: (same, diff) = (0, colors). The answer is same + diff after the last post, modulo 1,000,000,007. When there is a single color the formula correctly yields 0 for three or more posts. Time O(posts), space O(1).
